# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE)

## SECTION 0 — Overview

The honest value is a quarter of the price in Base and a third in Bull. Even the most aggressive defensible case ($369) is 66% below where the stock trades. This is not a "wait for a dip" situation — it is a price that demands ~107.8%/yr cash-flow growth in years 3–5 (the desk's price-implied figure under my structure), a rate almost no $1–10B company has ever sustained for a decade.

## SECTION 1 — Macro (DATA 1.5 / 1.6) and exposure
- **Rates:** nominal 10y **5.28%**, real 2.92%, breakeven 2.36%; curve +0.47% (steepening). COE ANCHOR **10.50%**. A high-multiple growth name is the most rate-sensitive asset class; every 100bp of required return compresses a 30–50x-forward multiple materially. [Actual]
- **Regime vector (2026-10-01):** goldilocks 0.341 / reflation 0.271 / tightening 0.176 / stagflation 0.130 / recession 0.081 — headline goldilocks but contested (margin 0.070). A ~30% probability mass on tightening/stagflation is a live tail for a stock priced for flawless execution. [Actual]
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` (severity 1, up, onset 2026-09-28) via Strait of Hormuz closure + Saudi pipeline attack; CPI 3.35% / PCE 3.42% YoY. Indirect exposure: higher energy/input costs for a fab-heavy manufacturer and a macro backdrop that keeps the Fed hawkish (news feed: "markets pricing possible additional rate hikes"). [Actual]
- **Demand driver:** hyperscaler AI capex is the single swing factor — record ~$725B combined 2026 budgets with all four signaling larger 2027 (InvestorPlace, 2026-05), but Goldman/Snider (2026) warn it will weigh on returns. This is both the Bull engine and the Bear's digestion trigger. [Estimate]

**Net:** macro is a headwind to the *multiple* (rates, vol, oil) while the *demand* story stays strong. That asymmetry — strong fundamentals, hostile multiple environment — is exactly why the price is doing the heavy lifting here.

## SECTION 2 — Business and moat
**Economic engines (Pillar 1 deconstruction):**
1. **Transactional deliveries (the bulk today):** Components ($2,005.6M FY26, +79.7%) and Systems ($1,008.4M, +90.7%) — optical chips, EML lasers, transceivers, OCS, industrial lasers. Cyclical hardware sold into cloud/AI/telecom. [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P2]
2. **Captive installed-base / annuity: WEAK.** No contracted backlog or recurring-revenue figure is disclosed in the filings (research brief confirms "no specific figures for units/GW/systems in field"; switching costs are low — components can be swapped by system vendors). I credit **no** multi-year annuity because the filings show no backlog/ARR to secure one. This is the key structural weakness vs. a Ciena-type installed base. [Assumption, supported by absence in PRIMARY P2]
3. **Strategic optionality (the re-rating driver):** CPO ultra-high-power lasers, initial ELS-module order, NPO engagements, OCS (first $100M+ quarter guided), and the die-to-die VCSEL interconnect (ECOC 2026). These "in-rack" penetration signals expand TAM beyond pluggables. [Actual for the announcements, PRIMARY P1; commercial magnitude Unconfirmed]

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** FY26 GAAP NI of **−$6,935M** is dominated by a **one-time, non-cash $7,756.6M loss on debt extinguishment** from equitizing convertibles (PRIMARY P1). Stripping that out: non-GAAP pre-tax $936.9M − non-GAAP tax $154.6M = **~$782M non-GAAP NI**, which has SBC ($191.3M) added back. Treating SBC as a real cost (deducted once, `sbc_treatment=deducted_in_cf`) gives FY26 owner earnings after SBC of **~$0.64B** — my Base base_cf. Note FY26 *cash* FCF was only $300M (OCF $751M − capex $451M) because the +83% revenue spike tied up working capital (receivables → $520M, inventory → $692M per PRIMARY P1 balance sheet); that is a one-off USE of cash, not the run-rate. [Actual inputs; $0.64B base = Estimate/Assumption]

**Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3 each, total /21 → 1.0–5.0):**
| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Intangibles / IP (InP, 200G EML, CPO lasers) | 2 | Real technical edge, hard to replicate |
| Switching costs | 1 | Low — components swappable by system vendors; CPO/OCS design-wins add some lock-in going forward |
| Network effects | 0 | None material |
| Cost advantage | 2 | Leading high-end laser fab; capacity effectively sold out through 2027 (supply IS the advantage now) |
| Efficient scale | 1 | Niche, not a protected duopoly (Coherent, Innolight, Eoptolink compete) |
| Brand / customer relationships | 2 | Nvidia $2B + purchase commitment; hyperscaler access |
| Installed base / recurring | 1 | Weak — no captive fleet annuity |
| **Total** | **9/21 → 2.8/5.0** | Direction: **improving** (CPO/OCS design-wins, Nvidia partnership) but narrow |

**Financial strength:** Effectively net-neutral to modestly net-cash. Cash + ST investments $2,738.4M vs total obligations ~$1,637M ($1,596.9M current-portion convertibles + $40.5M LT) → **~$1.1B net cash** if the converts are counted as debt; ~$2.7B if (more correctly) treated as equity-settling claims. Low leverage, ample liquidity to fund the capex ramp. Piotroski 5/9 (partial denominator). [Actual, PRIMARY P1 balance sheet]
